claim_1.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, and lung-draining lymph nodes showed distinct transcriptional profiles between CD56 bright CD16− and CD56 dim CD16+ NK cell subsets, with subset-specific gene expression conserved across sites.Principal component analysis (PCA) showed that CD56brightCD16− and CD56dimCD16+ NK cells formed distinct clusters across the sampled tissues, indicating that subset identity was a major source of transcriptional variation, while tissue site contributed additional variation within subsets.

sources.quote: Whole transcriptome profiling by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of CD56 bright CD16− and CD56 dim CD16+ NK cells sorted from blood, BM, spleen, lung, and LLN. Analysis of the whole transcriptome identified global signatures of 1,083 genes differentially expressed (DE) between CD56 bright CD16− and CD56 dim CD16+ NK cells (702 upregulated and 381 downregulated; Table S2) from these sites.

The global gene expression differences we identified between CD56 bright CD16− and CD56 dim CD16+ NK cells were conserved in all sites, revealing subset-specific profiles consistent with previous studies of NK subsets from single sites.

claim_2.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, and lung-draining lymph nodes showed that the global gene expression differences between CD56brightCD16− and CD56dimCD16+ NK cells were conserved across all sampled sites, revealing stable subset-specific transcriptional programs. CD56dimCD16+ NK cells showed higher expression of GZMB, GZMH, IFNG, KIR, S1PR5, S1PR1, CXCR1, CXCR2, and CX3CR1, whereas CD56brightCD16− NK cells showed higher expression of CD27, TNFSF4, TNFSF8, TNFSF13, TNFSF13B, CCR7, SELL, CXCR3, and CCR5.

sources.quote: The global gene expression differences we identified between CD56brightCD16− and CD56dimCD16+ NK cells were conserved in all sites, revealing subset-specific profiles consistent with previous studies of NK subsets from single sites.

Genes upregulated in CD56dimCD16+ NK cells include those associated with effector function (GZMB, GZMH, IFNG), killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIR), and tissue egress and circulation (S1PR5, S1PR1, CXCR1, CXCR2, and CX3CR1), while CD56brightCD16− NK cells express elevated levels of genes associated with immune regulation (CD27, TNFSF4, TNFSF8, TNFSF13, and TNFSF13B) and tissue homing (CCR7, SELL, CXCR3, and CCR5) (Figure S3B).

claim_3.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, and lung-draining lymph nodes from showed that CD56brightCD16− NK cells expressed higher levels of the transcription factors LEF1 and TCF7, which are associated with cellular stemness and quiescence, whereas CD56dimCD16+ NK cells expressed higher levels of the transcription factors TBX21, ZEB2, and IRF6, which are associated with terminal differentiation and effector function.

sources.quote: CD56brightCD16− NK cells expressed genes encoding transcription factors involved in cellular stemness and quiescence (Kuo and Leiden, 1999; Zhou et al., 2010) including LEF1 and TCF7 (TCF-1), while CD56dimCD16+ NK cells, expressed genes encoding transcription factors associated with terminal differentiation and effector function including TBX21 (T-bet), ZEB2, and IRF6 (Figure 4C).

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, gut, showed that CD45+ CD14− CD19− NK cells predominate in blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lungs, while CD56 bright CD16− NK cells are more prevalent in lymph nodes, tonsils and gut. This indicates that terminal differential of NK cells is more prevalent in blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung and excluded from lymph nodes and intestines.

sources.quote: The tissue distribution of NK cells among CD45+ CD14− CD19− cells was consistent between donors with blood, BM, spleen, and lung having significantly higher frequencies of NK cells (5%–50%) compared to low frequencies (<0.1%–2%) of NK cells in the LNs, tonsil, and gut.

The distribution of CD56 bright CD16− and CD56 dim CD16+ NK cell subsets was also a feature of the tissue site; CD56 bright CD16− NK cells predominated in LNs, tonsil, and gut while the majority of NK cells in blood, BM, spleen, and lung were CD56 dim CD16+.

claim_5.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, gut, lung-draining lymph node, and mesenteric lymph node from using SPADE projection identified distinct branches of CD56brightCD16− NK cells with site-specific variation in tissue-resident marker expression that was consistent across individual donors. CD69 expression was detected in the majority of CD56+ NK cells, except for a distinct branch of cells expressing the highest levels of CD56 that lacked CD69, consistent with a possible circulating immature NK-cell subset.

sources.quote: Spanning-tree progression analysis of density-normalized events (SPADE) (Qiu et al., 2011) projection of NK cells from blood, BM, spleen, lung, gut, LLN, and MLN identified distinct branches of CD56brightCD16− NK cells that exhibit site-specific variations in expression of tissue-resident markers, consistent between five individual donors (Figures 6A and S5C).

CD69 expression was detected in the majority of CD56+ NK cells, except for a specific branch of cells expressing the highest levels of CD56 that lack CD69 (Figures 6A and S5C), and may represent a circulating subset of immature NK cells.

claim_6.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, lung, tonsil, gut, and lymph node showed tissue-specific differences in FcεRIγ expression within the CD56dimCD16+ NK-cell subset. CD56dimCD16+ NK cells from tonsil, gut, and lymph node expressed substantially higher levels of FcεRIγ compared with CD56dimCD16+ NK cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lung.

claim_9.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of NK cells from bone marrow, spleen, lung, tonsil, gut, and lymph node showed subset- and site-specific variation in expression of the canonical tissue-resident memory surface markers CD69 and CD103. In bone marrow, spleen, lung, and tonsil, significantly higher frequencies of CD56brightCD16− NK cells expressed CD69 compared with CD56dimCD16+ NK cells, whereas in gut and lymph node the two NK-cell subsets showed comparable CD69 expression. In mucosal sitesl sites, including lung and intestine, substantial frequencies of CD69+ NK cells co-expressed CD103.

sources.quote: The expression of canonical TRM surface markers CD69 and CD103 by tissue NK cells showed subset- and site-specific variations.

In BM, spleen, lungs, and tonsils, CD69 was expressed by significantly higher frequencies (35%–90%) of CD56brightCD16− compared to CD56dimCD16+ NK cells; however, in gut and LN, CD56brightCD16− and CD56dimCD16+ NK cell subsets exhibited comparable CD69 expression (Figure 5C).
In mucosal sitesl sites (lungs, intestines) substantial frequencies of CD69+ NK cells co-expressed CD103 (Figure 5C).

claim_10.claim: Phenotypic analysis of NK cells from multiple tissue sites showed that the frequency and distribution of CD69 expression by CD56brightCD16− NK cells was not altered with age, consistent with tissue residence as an intrinsic property. Across tissues, CD56brightCD16− NK cells exhibited features of tissue residency, whereas CD56dimCD16+ NK cells showed signatures of circulating cells in blood, bone marrow, and spleen, but could adopt resident phenotypes in lymph node and mucosal sitesl sites.

sources.quote: The frequency and distribution of CD69 expression by CD56brightCD16− NK cells in tissues was not altered with age (Figure S5B), suggesting that tissue residence is an intrinsic property.

These findings show that CD56brightCD16− NK cells exhibit features of tissue residency in multiple sites, whereas CD56dimCD16+ NK cells bear signatures of circulating cells in blood, BM, and spleen, but can adopt resident phenotypes in LN and mucosal sitesl sites.

sources.quote: By contrast, immature subsets populating LLN and MLN contained the two precursor subsets (CD56brightCD127+CD161+) along with lower frequencies of five immature NK cell states (clusters 3–7) (Figure 7D; Table S6).

claim_12.claim: Flow cytometry analysis identified two NK-cell states in the gut that were absent or present only at low frequencies in other sites, appearing mainly in the gut and at low frequencies in the gut-draining mesenteric lymph node but not in lung-draining lymph node. Cluster 3 cells exhibited an NKp44+NKp46+CD160+CD294loNKG2A− phenotype, whereas cluster 4 cells exhibited an NKp44−NKp46−CD160−CD85j+ phenotype, consistent with intestinal-site-enriched NK-cell subsets.

sources.quote: Last, we identified only two NK cell states in the gut (clusters 3 and 4) that were not found in the other sites except for low frequencies, specifically in the gut-draining MLN, and not in LLN.
Cluster 3 cells exhibited a distinct NKp44+NKp46+CD160+CD294loNKG2A− phenotype, whereas cluster 4 cells lacked expression of NKp44, NKp46, and CD160, but exhibited upregulated expression of CD85j.

These distinct NK cell subsets appear to be specific or enriched within intestinal sites (and intestinal LN) because in the donors from whom we did not obtain intestinal tissues (donors 1–3; Figure 7B), these clusters were not observed.
